title: Eventual consistency, and the user who sees the old value

videos.script: The previous lesson ended with a choice. When a copy cannot be sure it is current, it can refuse, or it can answer with what it has. {{choice}} This lesson is about the second answer, and about the person who receives it. {{person}} Eventual consistency promises one thing: stop writing, wait, and every copy ends up with the same value. It does not say how long the wait is, or what anybody sees in the meantime. {{promise}} On your machine, Quitanda's shop keeps its own copy of the stock, fed by events. You will watch the copy lag behind, and the lag grow when the events pile up. {{lag}} Then the awkward cases. A member of staff changes a number and the page still shows the old one. A customer reloads and sees the number go backwards. {{backwards}} An event that arrives late and quietly undoes a newer one. And a basket edited in two places at once, where one of the edits disappears. {{basket}} Each one has a fix, and each fix is small once you can name the problem. Most of them come down to one idea: a version number that travels with the data.
